conviction_note: The quarter should land close to a thin consensus of $0.43 EPS and $43.0M revenue (one analyst). Sector evidence points both ways: Navigator's Q3 was soft for the smaller ships, while VLGC rates hit records. The stock trades at about net cash, after a related-party fleet deal it already sold off on (-5.07% on Nov 5) and the Gas Husky loss (-2.57% on Nov 18). What will move it is how the call handles capital, Gas Husky and coverage, not the EPS line. Findings sum to -0.35 and the scaled number is 0 (p_up 50, abs 3.0). The gap is the small negative lean on rates and coverage. The firm reason for a sign is missing, so p_up stays at 50.

expectations.real_bar: The quarter is a wash. To rise, the stock needs the call to answer the discount to cash: a buyback, a softer or re-priced related-party deal, a Gas Husky loss fully covered by war-risk insurance with no further Black Sea exposure, or firmer 2027 coverage. Absent that, a second consecutive quarter of lower earnings on a shrinking fleet keeps it pinned near cash.

findings.finding: Thin consensus of $0.43 EPS / $43.0M revenue against a run-rate that is drifting down: Q2 adjusted EPS was $0.46 on revenue of $42.9M with 26.4 average vessels. Q3 has a smaller fleet (the $10.5M held-for-sale vessel delivered in Q3), higher bunker costs on spot voyages, and Q2 operational utilisation already at 82.3% from idle small ships. Offsetting that, interest income rises on cash that went from $168M to more than $250M. Expect revenue slightly below $43.0M and adjusted EPS around $0.40-0.46.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a miss of $0.46 against $0.50 traded about -2%. Q3 2025: a miss of $0.39 against $0.46 traded about +1.2% (baseline 2025-11-25 row). Q1 2026: a beat of $0.40 against $0.33, with no large move recorded. This name does not pay much for the EPS line.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus comes from a single analyst and has not visibly been revised since September. If the market expected a revenue miss, it would already discount it, and on this name's history a miss moves it about 2% at most. Small by construction.
findings.independence: The consensus figure is from https://www.investing.com/equities/stealthgas-earnings. The softer Q3 for small-ship peers is from a different source (Navigator, below).

findings.finding: Navigator Holdings (reported 2026-11-03/04) had a soft Q3 2026. TCE fell to $30,314/day from $33,946 in Q2, utilisation fell to 87.9% from 90.8%, and customers paused in July-August on US-Iran headlines. Utilisation rebounded to 94% in September, and semi-refrigerated LPG rates were 'firming' into Q4.
findings.link: Navigator's handysize semi-refrigerated and ethylene fleet overlaps GASS's handysize ships (GASS has two handysize in the spot market, per the Q2 call) and the same Q3 calendar. Most of GASS's fleet is smaller pressurised ships that Navigator does not operate, so the overlap is partial.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No GASS reaction to a peer print is recorded. NVGS itself fell 7.2% after its report.
findings.why_not_priced: GASS's consensus has not been touched since September. The Navigator print came after GASS last spoke (2026-09-02). If it were priced, the single estimate would have moved.
findings.independence: Proxy only. https://www.panabee.com/news/navigator-earnings-q3-2026 is the same print.

findings.finding: Dorian LPG's quarter ended 2026-09-30 set records: TCE of $96,990 per available day (+80.5%) on the effective closure of Hormuz and longer US-Asia voyages, offset partly by VLSFO bunkers at $826/t against $505. The large-ship market was very strong through Q3.
findings.link: Weak: GASS has no VLGCs. The Q2 release said TCE 'improved for larger vessels' (its MGC/handysize units), and the Q2 call said MGC swap rates were at levels 'never seen before'. The bunker cost hits GASS's spot voyages the same way.
findings.why_not_priced: The read-through to GASS's few larger ships is not in the single estimate. It is a proxy, sized small.
findings.independence: None for GASS specifically. It partly offsets the Navigator finding.

findings.finding: Possible Q3 GAAP gain on the Eco Wizard insurance claim. Claims receivable was $64.2M at June 30, 2026 (Q2 balance sheet). The Q2 call put the settlement received in July at about $77M. If the receivable is the Eco Wizard claim, Q3 GAAP carries a gain of roughly $12.8M (about $0.34 per share), and headline GAAP EPS could print around $0.75 against $0.43. Adjusted EPS would likely exclude it. The July 7 release says the damaged hull will be sold 'with no monetary gain', which concerns the hull sale, not the claim.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior GAAP one-off reaction for this name was found. Q2's $1.3M vessel-sale gain drew no comment.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview or aggregator carries an insurance gain, and the $0.43 consensus is a run-rate figure. If it were priced, the consensus would sit well above the run-rate. The path to the multiple is cash already counted (>$270M), so this is a fraction of the same money as operating profit.
findings.independence: The roughly $77M figure is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15511681835148288), a different document from the balance sheet. Whether the receivable is entirely Eco Wizard is an inference.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-05 the company agreed to buy four LPG carriers (two 40,000 cbm, two 11,000 cbm, delivering May-Sep 2027, charter-free) for $254.6M from entities affiliated with CEO Harry Vafias's family. That is almost all of the more than $270M cash, against a market cap of about $287M (37.92M shares at $7.58). The price is the average of independent valuations, there is no fairness opinion, and Stealth Maritime earns a 1% fee. The stock fell 5.07% that day. The Q3 call is the first time management faces questions on it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-11-05: -5.07% on the announcement (baseline row). The Q2 call said no buyback because the price had risen; $21M has been bought back since 2023.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal itself is priced (-5% plus the drift to about 1.0x cash). What is unpriced is any change on the call: a buyback alongside it, a deferral, or a defence that adds nothing. Sized near zero with a wide range, because the sign depends on what management says.
findings.independence: Proxy statement, special meeting 2026-12-11 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1328919/000119312526450866/d119196dex991.htm), the same transaction. Governance-risk commentary at https://www.panabee.com/news/stealthgas-plans-255-million-fleet-expansion-via-related-party-deal.

findings.finding: The setup is depressed. Spot $7.58 is about 19% below the post-Q2 $9.33, 27% below the 52-week high, 46% below the only target ($14), and market cap of about $287M sits near cash of more than $270M with zero debt (6-K 2026-11-05) and a 25-vessel fleet. The real bar for a rise is low in price terms, but the overhang (the related-party deal) is structural.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 print about -2% from about $9.50. No record of a relief rally at a discount like this.
findings.why_not_priced: A discount to cash is visible to everyone, and the market is applying it deliberately because of the related-party deal. Only a call that changes the use of cash would close it. Sized small.
findings.independence: TowerView's 13D/A letter makes the same undervaluation argument (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1328919/000114036126028176/xslSCHEDULE_13D_X02/primary_doc.xml).

findings.finding: Gas Husky (2012-built, about 7,200 dwt, on time charter to Mar 2027) was struck in the Black Sea about 50nm off Bulgaria on 2026-11-17 and appears to have sunk. All 19 crew are safe. The company's 6-K of 2026-11-18 says the vessel's condition is 'unknown'. The Q3 call is the first chance to give the insurance position (war-risk cover) and Black Sea exposure. It is the second StealthGas hull lost to an attack in 17 months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-11-18: -2.57% (baseline row). Eco Wizard (July 2025) ended in a full insurance settlement of about $77M in July 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The loss is priced (-2.57%). What is not priced is the insurance answer. 'Fully insured at above book' would be a small positive, and 'trading pattern exposed to the Black Sea' a negative. Net about zero with a downside tail.
findings.independence: Riviera, 2026-11-17, says it appears to have sunk (https://www.rivieramm.com/news-content-hub/greek-owned-lpg-carrier-appears-to-have-sunk-in-black-sea-in-second-incident-in-two-days-90600). Maritime Executive, 2026-11-17 (https://maritime-executive.com/article/crew-rescued-from-sinking-lpg-tanker-off-bulgaria-as-pace-of-attacks-grows).

findings.finding: Holder pressure for capital return. TowerView (7.3%) wrote to the board on 2026-07-08 asking it to consider liquidating and returning capital, and Glendon Capital disclosed 10.85% (13G/A filed 2026-11-13). The related-party deal goes the other way, so the call may carry questions or an announced buyback to placate holders.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None recorded for activist letters on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The letter is four months old and the company answered it with an acquisition, so any buyback announced on the call would be a surprise. Low probability.
findings.independence: Glendon 13G/A (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1328919/000160435026000028/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml) is passive and does not itself point the same way.

findings.finding: The coverage update, GASS's equivalent of guidance, is likely flat to down. At Q2 it was 60% of remaining 2026 days, about $30M secured for 2027, 45% one-year-forward, and total $90M, which management called 'slightly below where we would like'. Charterers were hesitant to commit. Gas Husky's charter to Mar 2027 is presumably lost. The four new vessels deliver charter-free in 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 coverage drop (from about $104M total at Q4 to about $90M at Q2) coincided with a -2% print reaction. No isolated reading is available.
findings.why_not_priced: No one publishes a coverage estimate. A further decline would show the earnings base shrinking while cash is committed to the deal. Small.
findings.independence: Navigator noted a cut in the 12-month TC assessment for ethylene handysize (https://finviz.com/news/416172/...), so period rates are softening at the margin.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew or implied move. The 20-day run-up of -6.5% and the post-Q2 slide of -19% fit a market that has already marked down the deal and Gas Husky. The small negative lean in the findings on rates and coverage runs with the run-up, and the depressed setup cuts against it, so p_up stays at 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs): the Eco Wizard insurance-gain finding went from +0.4 to +0.25, because it sits below the line with no path to the guide.
Lessons 6 and 1: the bar has two agreeing sources but one analyst, and this name has not paid for the EPS line, so the consensus finding was left small at -0.3. No further cut.
